How is LOTO applied?

Safe Energy Isolation in 6 Steps

Equipment is only useful together with the right procedure. You can find the details in our LOTO guide.

Preparation

Identify the machine's energy sources and isolation points.

Notice

Inform all affected employees about the shutdown.

Shut-off

Shut down the equipment using the normal stopping procedure.

Isolation

Cut energy off at its source with circuit breakers, valves and connections.

Lock + Tag

Each worker fits their own lock and personal tag.

Verification

Verify the zero-energy state by attempting to start the equipment.

FAQ

Frequently asked questions about LOTO

If you cannot find the answer you are looking for, you can reach us by phone or WhatsApp.

Contact us
What is LOTO?
Lockout/Tagout, known in Turkish as Energy Control Tagging and Lockout, is the safety procedure in which a machine's energy is cut off and locked out during maintenance, repair and cleaning to prevent unexpected start-up.
Which padlock should I choose?
For electrical work, locks with non-conductive plastic shackles are recommended; for general use, locks with steel shackles. A 38 mm shackle fits most lockout devices; on hasps, a 76 mm shackle is more comfortable to use.
Can the padlocks be opened with the same key?
Yes. We can prepare keyed-different (each lock with its own key), keyed-alike (a group of locks with one key) and master-keyed systems.
How do I find the right lock for my circuit breaker?
Just send the brand/model of your circuit breaker or a clear photo via WhatsApp, and we will tell you the suitable lockout equipment.
What is the delivery time?
In-stock products are usually shipped the same day or the next business day. For bulk orders, we provide lead time information together with the quote.
Do you issue invoices and take bulk orders?
We sell with corporate invoicing; for bulk purchases and sets we prepare a custom price quote for you.

Since 2010 we have been supplying industrial facilities with LOTO lockout and tagout equipment. Our products comply with the requirements of OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147.
